The event is a "vendor demo" (title/description indicates a demo involving a vendor).
The event has a Google Meet conferencing link attached.
The event has a room booked (a location/room resource).
The action requested is to move the event's start time to 3pm local time on that same day, presumably preserving its original duration.

The most recent past Thursday (far less likely but technically possible)

turn2.differences: The author's c1-c5 map cleanly onto my step-1 conditions (vendor demo -> c1, Thursday -> c2, confirmed status -> c3, Google Meet link -> c4, room booked -> c5). The 'move to 3pm' action is correctly excluded from the selection conditions since it's the update to perform, not a filter. No meaningful gaps between the author's list and my own reading.

ambiguity_effects.explain: All vendor-demo candidates (and the team sync event) fall on the same date, 2018-06-21, so reading 'Thursday' as this-coming-Thursday vs. any other Thursday doesn't change which records are in play here.

Under the natural reading (event.status field == 'confirmed'), ev_demo_target passes and is the sole match. Under a stricter alternate reading (all attendees, including the room resource, have responded 'accepted'), ev_demo_target would also fail, since its room-2b resource attendee shows 'needsAction' - a status that persists indefinitely for rooms in this data. That reading would eliminate the only match, but it's an unnatural way to read 'confirmed' for a meeting and isn't consistent with how calendar room resources normally behave, so it shouldn't be adopted.

Under the natural reading (a room resource attendee is present), ev_demo_target, ev_demo_tentative, and ev_demo_location_link all satisfy this. Under an alternate reading (the event's location text names a room), none of the records qualify, since the only populated location field (on ev_demo_location_link) contains a fake Meet URL, not a room name. This alternate reading would eliminate the intended match, but resource-attendee is the standard/expected signal for 'room booked' in this data model, so it's the reading a colleague would take.
All four demo-type events are literally titled 'Vendor demo', so reading this as an exact title match vs. a thematic match makes no difference here.
This ambiguity affects only how the update should be performed once the target event is identified, not which record is selected as 'Thursday's vendor demo.'

turn2.naturalness_note: The request reads like a realistic, naturally-phrased disambiguation: Jordan is distinguishing the real vendor demo from several look-alike decoys on the same day (a tentative duplicate, one with a fake Meet link in the location text instead of a real conferencing attachment, and one missing the room booking). The qualifiers given (confirmed, Meet link, room booked) are exactly the details needed to single out ev_demo_target, which is a natural way someone would describe a meeting to distinguish it from similar clutter on their calendar.
